textos.texto: Hi! My name is Carla. I am 28 years old and I am from Recife. Now I live in Rio. I am a nurse. My husband is Pedro. He is a teacher. We have a dog. His name is Max. Max is small and very happy. Our apartment is near the beach. I love my city!
perguntas: What is the dog's name? What is he like?
pessoais: Introduce yourself like Carla.
Do you have a pet? Tell me about it.

textos.texto: Tom wakes up at six o'clock. He takes a shower and has breakfast. He eats bread and drinks coffee. He goes to work by bus. He works in an office from nine to five. He has lunch at noon. In the evening, he watches TV and goes to bed at eleven.
perguntas: What time does Tom wake up?
What does he have for breakfast?
How does he go to work?
What time does he have lunch?
What does he do in the evening?
pessoais: What time do you wake up on Mondays?
How is your Monday different from Tom's?

textos.texto: I live in Botafogo. It is a busy neighborhood. There are many restaurants and bars, and there is a big shopping mall. There is a subway station near my building, so it is easy to go to work. There isn't a beach for swimming, but there is a beautiful view of Sugarloaf Mountain. On Saturdays, there is a street market on my street. I usually buy fruit there.
perguntas: What is there near the building?
Why is it easy to go to work?
Can you swim at the beach there?
pessoais: What is there in your neighborhood?
What is missing in your neighborhood?

textos.texto: The Silva family is very talented. Marcos, the father, can play the guitar and sing. His wife, Ana, can paint beautiful pictures. Their daughter, Bia, is ten. She can dance very well, but she can't sing. Their son, Leo, is six. He can't read yet, but he can draw animals. Their grandmother can cook amazing food. Every Sunday, the family has a small show at home.
perguntas: How old is Leo? What can he do?
pessoais: What can you do well?
Who is the most talented person in your family?

textos.texto: Julia is a doctor, and she always tries to have healthy habits. She usually wakes up early and goes running three times a week. She never drinks soda, and she hardly ever eats fast food. She sometimes eats chocolate on weekends. Julia drinks a lot of water every day. But she has a problem: she often works at night, so she doesn't always sleep eight hours. She says sleep is the most difficult habit for her.
perguntas: How often does she go running?
What is her biggest problem? Why?
pessoais: How often do you exercise?
Which healthy habit is difficult for you?

textos.texto: Last weekend, I was in Paraty with my friends. The weather was perfect: it was sunny and hot. Our hotel was small but very nice, and the people there were friendly. On Saturday, we were on a boat all day. The water was clear and warm. The restaurants were a little expensive, but the food was delicious. On Sunday night, we were very tired, but we were happy. It was a great weekend!
perguntas: Where was the person last weekend?
How were they on Sunday night?
pessoais: Where were you last weekend?
What was your best weekend this year?

textos.texto: It's four o'clock on a Friday afternoon at the Lima family's house. Mrs. Lima usually works at the hospital on Fridays, but today she is at home because she is sick. She is lying on the sofa and watching a movie. Her husband is cooking dinner, which is unusual — he normally orders pizza on Fridays. Their son, Davi, is doing his homework in his room. Actually, he isn't doing homework. He is playing video games!
perguntas: Why is Mrs. Lima at home today?
What does Mr. Lima usually do on Fridays?
pessoais: What do you usually do on Friday afternoons?
What is your family doing right now?

textos.texto: Last year, Rafael flew to Lisbon for a work conference. When he arrived at the airport, he waited for his suitcase, but it didn't come. He went to the airline desk and explained the problem. The woman there was very nice. She told him that his suitcase was in Madrid! Rafael had only his backpack, so he bought new clothes in a shop near the hotel. Two days later, the suitcase arrived. Rafael laughed — the conference was already over.
perguntas: Why did Rafael go to Lisbon?
Why did he laugh at the end?
pessoais: Have you ever had a problem at an airport?
What do you always take in your hand luggage?

textos.texto: Marina grew up in São Paulo, the biggest city in South America. Three years ago, she moved to a small town in Minas Gerais. 'Life here is slower and cheaper,' she says. 'My house is bigger than my old apartment, and the air is much cleaner.' But not everything is better. The nearest hospital is forty minutes away, and the internet is worse than in the city. 'I miss the restaurants and the cinemas,' she admits. 'But I'm happier here. It's the best decision I've ever made.'
perguntas: What is better in her new town? Give two things.
What is worse? Give two things.
Is she happy with her decision?
pessoais: Would you prefer to live in a big city or a small town? Why?
Compare your city with another place you know.

textos.texto: Sofia and her husband are going to travel to the Northeast in January. They've already booked the flights to Fortaleza, and they're going to rent a car to visit the beaches. Sofia wants to try kitesurfing, but her husband isn't sure. 'I think it'll be too difficult for me,' he says. They haven't decided where to stay on the last two days. 'Maybe we'll go to Jericoacoara,' says Sofia. 'Everybody says it's beautiful. I'm sure we'll love it.'
perguntas: When are they going to travel?
How are they going to visit the beaches?
What does her husband think about kitesurfing?
pessoais: What are your plans for your next vacation?
Would you try kitesurfing? Why or why not?

textos.texto: It was a hot night in February. I was working late at home and my wife was reading in bed. Suddenly, the wind started to blow very hard and the lights went out. While I was looking for a flashlight, I heard a loud noise in the kitchen. A tree branch was hitting the window! We didn't sleep much that night. In the morning, while we were having breakfast, a neighbor knocked on the door. Half of the street had no electricity, but nobody was hurt.
perguntas: What were the two people doing when the storm started?
What was the noise in the kitchen?
pessoais: What were you doing the last time it rained very hard?
Are you afraid of storms?

textos.texto: Starting a new job can be stressful. Here is some advice from people who have changed jobs many times. First, you should arrive a little early in the first week — you don't have to be the first one there, but you mustn't be late. Second, you should ask questions. Nobody expects you to know everything. Third, try to learn your colleagues' names quickly. Finally, you don't have to say yes to everything. If you have too much work, you should talk to your manager.
perguntas: Who gives the advice in the text?
What is the advice about arriving?
What should you do if you have too much work?
pessoais: What advice would you give to a new colleague at your job?
Have you ever started a new job? How was it?
